people.story: Howard Frank Magwire was born on New Year's Day 1919 in Springfield, Vermont, one of twin boys born that morning to Frank A. Magwire and Alice (Bates) Magwire; his twin was Harold Charles. The town's own printed register of births for 1919 lists the two boys one above the other. Howard grew up in a family well known in Springfield: his father ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield for thirty seven years. On October 16, 1940, aged 21, he registered for the draft, living at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, with his mother Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire as the person who would always know his address, and working at the Fellows Gear Shaper Company on River Street. A Veterans Affairs listing shows Army service from August 15, 1943 to January 7, 1946. By 1967 Howard was living in West Springfield, Massachusetts. On January 7, 1961 he married Gwendolyn Farr in Springfield, Vermont, and their daughter Tracy married Rick Crosby. Gwendolyn died before him. Howard died on September 26, 2014 (the Veterans Affairs listing gives the day) and was laid to rest in Oakland Cemetery in Springfield, beside his parents' lot. [^s01] [^s10] [^s13] [^s61] [^s63]
people.story_de: Howard Frank Magwire wurde am Neujahrstag 1919 in Springfield, Vermont, geboren, einer von zwei Zwillingsjungen, die an jenem Morgen als Kinder von Frank A. Magwire und Alice (Bates) Magwire zur Welt kamen; sein Zwilling war Harold Charles. Das eigene gedruckte Geburtsregister der Gemeinde für 1919 führt die beiden Jungen untereinander auf. Howard wuchs in einer in Springfield wohlbekannten Familie auf: sein Vater führte Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield siebenunddreißig Jahre lang. Am 16. Oktober 1940 meldete er sich im Alter von 21 Jahren zur Musterung. Er wohnte in der 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, gab seine Mutter Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire als die Person an, die seine Anschrift immer wissen würde, und arbeitete bei der Fellows Gear Shaper Company in der River Street. Ein Eintrag von Veterans Affairs zeigt Armeedienst vom 15. August 1943 bis zum 7. Januar 1946. 1967 wohnte Howard in West Springfield, Massachusetts. Am 7. Januar 1961 heiratete er Gwendolyn Farr in Springfield, Vermont, und die Tochter der beiden, Tracy, heiratete Rick Crosby. Gwendolyn starb vor ihm. Howard starb am 26. September 2014 (der Eintrag von Veterans Affairs nennt den Tag) und wurde im Oakland Cemetery in Springfield beigesetzt, neben der Grabstelle seiner Eltern. [^s01] [^s10] [^s13] [^s61] [^s63]

people.story: Gwendolyn Farr was born in Springfield, Vermont, in 1927, a daughter of Harry James Farr and Mary Abbie (West) Farr; her brother Richard's 2009 obituary names those parents. Family tradition: West cousins remembered summer visits with Aunt Abby and Uncle Harry. That memory is not on the map. On January 7, 1961 she married Howard Frank Magwire in Springfield, and they made their home in West Springfield, Massachusetts. Their daughter is Tracy Jo Crosby. Gwen loved quilting, knitting and sewing, walks with her husband and coffee with friends, and was remembered for her ever present smile. After many years of congestive heart failure she died at Suffield, Connecticut, on September 6, 2009, after 48 years of marriage. Services were private. [^s36] [^s27] [^s10] Her Vermont birth record, found in November 2026, confirms that she was born on July 1, 1927 at Springfield Hospital, the first child of Harry J. Farr and M. Abbie West. [^s50]
people.story_de: Gwendolyn Farr wurde 1927 in Springfield, Vermont, geboren, eine Tochter von Harry James Farr und Mary Abbie (West) Farr; der Nachruf ihres Bruders Richard von 2009 nennt diese Eltern. Familientradition: Cousinen und Cousins der Familie West erinnerten sich an Sommerbesuche bei Tante Abby und Onkel Harry. Diese Erinnerung ist nicht auf der Karte. Am 7. Januar 1961 heiratete sie Howard Frank Magwire in Springfield, und sie machten West Springfield, Massachusetts, zu ihrem Zuhause. Die Tochter der beiden ist Tracy Jo Crosby. Gwen liebte Quilten, Stricken und Nähen, Spaziergänge mit ihrem Mann und Kaffee mit Freunden und wurde wegen ihres stets vorhandenen Lächelns in Erinnerung behalten. Nach vielen Jahren der kongestiven Herzinsuffizienz starb sie am 6. September 2009 in Suffield, Connecticut, nach 48 Ehejahren. Die Trauerfeier war privat. [^s36] [^s27] [^s10] Ihr Geburtsbeleg aus Vermont, gefunden im November 2026, bestätigt, dass sie am 1. Juli 1927 im Springfield Hospital geboren wurde, als erstes Kind von Harry J. Farr und M. Abbie West. [^s50]

people.story: Frank Albert Magwire was born on February 14, 1889 in Springfield, Vermont, the son of Albert A. Magwire and Alice Jenny (Spaulding) Magwire. He graduated from Springfield High School in 1909 and on July 10, 1912 he married Alice Evadna Bates in Springfield; the marriage appears in the town's printed register for that year. In June 1917 he registered for the draft at Woodsville, New Hampshire, aged 28, as a druggist supporting a wife and one child, and described as short and slender with light gray eyes and brown hair. He trained as a pharmacist and registered in Vermont, and in 1914, while working in Charlestown, New Hampshire, just across the Connecticut River, he was granted a New Hampshire license by reciprocity. For thirty seven years Frank owned and ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield, retiring in 1954. In 1940 he kept three state licensed pinball machines in the store, and when the village demanded its own large license fee he paid under protest and sued; in January 1941 the Vermont Supreme Court reversed the dismissal of his suit and sent it back for trial. He belonged to St. John's Lodge No. 41 F&AM and Independent Order of Odd Fellows Lodge No. 42 for more than fifty years, was a 32nd Degree Mason and a member of Mt. Sinai Shrine in Montpelier. Frank and Alice raised three sons: Raymond (born 1913) and the twins Harold and Howard (born January 1, 1919). Frank died at Springfield Hospital on October 8, 1967 and was buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s02] [^s13] [^s18] [^s43] [^s53] In October 1940 all three of his sons named him or his wife as the person who would always know their address, at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield. [^s60] [^s61] [^s62]
people.story_de: Frank Albert Magwire wurde am 14. Februar 1889 in Springfield, Vermont, geboren, der Sohn von Albert A. Magwire und Alice Jenny (Spaulding) Magwire. Er schloss 1909 die Springfield High School ab und heiratete am 10. Juli 1912 in Springfield Alice Evadna Bates; die Eheschließung erscheint im gedruckten Register der Town für jenes Jahr. Im Juni 1917 meldete er sich in Woodsville, New Hampshire, im Alter von 28 Jahren zur Musterung, als Apotheker, der eine Ehefrau und ein Kind unterhielt, und wurde als klein und schlank beschrieben, mit hellgrauen Augen und braunem Haar. Er wurde zum Apotheker ausgebildet und ließ sich in Vermont registrieren, und 1914, während er in Charlestown, New Hampshire, unmittelbar jenseits des Connecticut River arbeitete, erhielt er durch Gegenseitigkeit eine Zulassung von New Hampshire. Siebenunddreißig Jahre lang besaß und betrieb Frank Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield und ging 1954 in den Ruhestand. 1940 hielt er drei vom Bundesstaat zugelassene Flipperautomaten im Laden, und als das Dorf eine eigene hohe Lizenzgebühr verlangte, zahlte er unter Protest und klagte; im Januar 1941 hob der Vermont Supreme Court die Abweisung seiner Klage auf und verwies die Sache zur Verhandlung zurück. Er gehörte mehr als fünfzig Jahre der St. John's Lodge No. 41 F&AM und der Independent Order of Odd Fellows Lodge No. 42 an, war Freimaurer des 32. Grades und Mitglied im Mt. Sinai Shrine in Montpelier. Frank und Alice zogen drei Söhne groß: Raymond (geboren 1913) und die Zwillinge Harold und Howard (geboren am 1. Januar 1919). Frank starb am 8. Oktober 1967 im Springfield Hospital und wurde auf dem Oakland Cemetery beigesetzt. [^s02] [^s13] [^s18] [^s43] [^s53] Im Oktober 1940 nannten alle drei seiner Söhne ihn oder seine Ehefrau, 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, als die Person, die ihre Anschrift immer kennen würde. [^s60] [^s61] [^s62]

people.story: Alice Evadna Bates was born on September 7, 1889 in Williamstown, Massachusetts. She married Frank Albert Magwire in Springfield, Vermont, on July 10, 1912, and spent the rest of her life in Springfield, where she raised sons Raymond, Harold and Howard. She died on March 29, 1972 and is buried with Frank in Oakland Cemetery. Her own parents have not yet been identified; her Williamstown birth record has been requested. [^s02] [^s14] [^s13] Her son Howard's 1940 draft card names Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire, mother, at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield. [^s61]
people.story_de: Alice Evadna Bates wurde am 7. September 1889 in Williamstown, Massachusetts, geboren. Sie heiratete Frank Albert Magwire am 10. Juli 1912 in Springfield, Vermont, und verbrachte den Rest ihres Lebens in Springfield, wo sie die Söhne Raymond, Harold und Howard aufzog. Sie starb am 29. März 1972 und ist mit Frank im Oakland Cemetery begraben. Ihre eigenen Eltern sind noch nicht ermittelt; ihr Geburtsbeleg aus Williamstown wurde angefordert. [^s02] [^s14] [^s13] Die Musterungskarte ihres Sohnes Howard von 1940 nennt Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire, Mutter, in der 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield. [^s61]

people.story: Albert A. Magwire was born on October 10, 1845 in Brooklyn, New York. His 1887 marriage card names his parents as George and Mary (Prentis), and his 1929 death card gives his mother's maiden name as Mary Prentiss and his father as unknown, so George is probable and Mary is firm. On November 8, 1887, a musician aged 40 on his second marriage, he married Alice J. Spaulding; the card was recorded at Springfield, Vermont, which settles an earlier note that said Cavendish. They made their home in Springfield, where their children Ethel, Frank Albert, Edna, Charles E. and Harrold were born. Albert was in the music trade: in 1904 he ran the Springfield Music Rooms as an Edison phonograph dealer, gave twice weekly outdoor evening phonograph concerts that August, and on October 25, 1904 gave a ticketed phonograph concert in Ludlow Town Hall with two young pianists. Albert died in Springfield on February 21, 1929, aged 83 years, 4 months and 11 days, a music teacher, and is buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s15] [^s16] [^s18] [^s13] [^s44] [^s58] [^s59]
people.story_de: Albert A. Magwire wurde am 10. Oktober 1845 in Brooklyn, New York, geboren. Seine Heiratskarte von 1887 nennt seine Eltern als George und Mary (Prentis), und seine Sterbekarte von 1929 gibt den Mädchennamen seiner Mutter als Mary Prentiss an und seinen Vater als unbekannt, sodass George wahrscheinlich ist und Mary feststeht. Am 8. November 1887 heiratete er, als Musiker von 40 Jahren in zweiter Ehe, Alice J. Spaulding; die Karte wurde in Springfield, Vermont, eingetragen, was eine frühere Notiz klärt, die Cavendish nannte. Sie machten Springfield zu ihrem Wohnsitz, wo ihre Kinder Ethel, Frank Albert, Edna, Charles E. und Harrold geboren wurden. Albert war im Musikhandel tätig: 1904 betrieb er die Springfield Music Rooms als Händler für Edison-Phonographen, gab in jenem August zweimal wöchentlich abendliche Phonographenkonzerte im Freien und am 25. Oktober 1904 ein Phonographenkonzert mit Eintrittskarten in der Ludlow Town Hall mit zwei jungen Pianisten. Albert starb am 21. Februar 1929 in Springfield im Alter von 83 Jahren, 4 Monaten und 11 Tagen, von Beruf Musiklehrer, und ist auf dem Oakland Cemetery begraben. [^s15] [^s16] [^s18] [^s13] [^s44] [^s58] [^s59]

people.story: Alice Jenny Spaulding was born on August 17, 1866 in Cavendish, Vermont, the fourth daughter of Charles Elliot and Amantha (Putnam) Spaulding. Two separate family histories, the Spalding Memorial of 1872 and the Dickey Genealogy of 1898, list her birth date. She married Albert A. Magwire in Cavendish in November 1887 and raised her family in Springfield. She died on November 13, 1951 in West Lebanon, New Hampshire, and was buried with Albert in Oakland Cemetery, Springfield. people.story: Charles Elliot Spaulding was born on July 24, 1833 and married Amantha Putnam in Springfield, Vermont, on March 25, 1856. He farmed in Cavendish, where the couple raised Addie Cora, Ida Jenny (who died young), Anna Emma, Alice Jenny, Frank Charles, Lilla May and Gertie Inez. The Spalding Memorial of 1872 traces him eight generations back to Edward Spalding, the immigrant ancestor of the American Spaldings; that pedigree is still a lead. Charles died on March 26, 1890 and is buried in Cavendish Village Cemetery. [^s06] [^s07] [^s17]

people.story: Amantha Putnam was born on September 9, 1837, a daughter of Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall according to the Dickey Genealogy. She married Charles Elliot Spaulding in Springfield, Vermont, in 1856 and lived in Cavendish for most of her life. She outlived her husband by thirty six years, dying in Proctorsville on May 30, 1926, and rests beside him in Cavendish Village Cemetery. Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall are named only in that compiled genealogy, so they are not drawn on the tree. [^s07] [^s06] [^s17]

people.story: Raymond Bates Magwire, the eldest son of Frank and Alice Magwire, was born in Springfield, Vermont, on March 18, 1913. In 1936 he was a junior at Springfield College in Massachusetts. On October 16, 1940, aged 27, he registered for the draft from 1 Capitol Hill, Fair Haven, Vermont, as a student at Springfield College, naming his father Frank Albert Magwire, of 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, as the person who would always know his address. He served as a private first class in the U.S. Army in the Second World War. He made a career in physical education, and by 1952 he was Vermont's state director of health and physical education in the State Department of Education at Montpelier, where he was still living in 1967. He died on April 26, 1997, in Rutland according to Find a Grave, and is buried in Hillside Cemetery, which a Veterans gravesite record lists as at Fair Haven and which is physically in Castleton. His Social Security claims index entry names his parents as Frank A. Magwire and Alice Bates. [^s12] [^s13] [^s45] [^s46] [^s62] [^s64] [^s65]

Er diente im Zweiten Weltkrieg als Private First Class in der U.S. Army. Er machte Karriere in der Leibeserziehung, und spätestens 1952 war er staatlicher Direktor für Gesundheit und Leibeserziehung von Vermont im State Department of Education in Montpelier, wo er 1967 noch lebte. Er starb laut Find a Grave am 26. April 1997 in Rutland und ist auf dem Hillside Cemetery begraben, den ein Veteranen-Grabstättenbeleg als in Fair Haven gelegen verzeichnet und der physisch in Castleton liegt. Sein Eintrag im Social Security Claims Index nennt seine Eltern als Frank A. Magwire und Alice Bates. [^s12] [^s13] [^s45] [^s46] [^s62] [^s64] [^s65]

people.story: Harry James Farr was born in Denver, Colorado, on April 3, 1888, the son of George Oscar Farr (born in Westfield, Massachusetts) and Alice Beard (born in Andover, Vermont), according to his 1926 marriage card and his 1966 death certificate. He served a year as a corporal in the Vermont National Guard and was discharged in July 1913. On December 4, 1912 he married Laura Mary Seward in Springfield, Vermont; that marriage ended in divorce. By June 1917 he was a letter carrier for the U.S. Post Office in Bridgeport, Connecticut, living at 276 Gregory Street. He was back in Springfield by 1926, and on August 11, 1926, at Chester, Vermont, he married Mary Abbie West of Chester Depot. Their daughter Gwendolyn was born in 1927, Richard in 1930, and Alma later. In 1942 he lived at 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, and worked for the U.S. Post Office Department on Main Street, Springfield; in 1950 he was 62 and living in Springfield. The card that follows his 1942 card in the Vermont set, probably the back of it, describes a man 5 feet 7 inches tall and 142 pounds, with blue eyes and brown hair. He died at DeGoesbriand Memorial Hospital, Burlington, Vermont, on May 22, 1966, aged 78, retired and residing at 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, and his death certificate names his wife as Mary Abbie. Family tradition: the family remembered summer days at a West farm in Wells, Maine. That place is only a lead, so it is not on the map. [^s05] [^s03] [^s27] [^s41] [^s42] [^s48] [^s49] [^s52] [^s55] [^s57] [^s66]
people.story_de: Harry James Farr wurde am 3. April 1888 in Denver, Colorado, als Sohn von George Oscar Farr (geboren in Westfield, Massachusetts) und Alice Beard (geboren in Andover, Vermont) geboren, laut seiner Heiratskarte von 1926 und seiner Sterbeurkunde von 1966. Er diente ein Jahr als Korporal in der Vermont National Guard und wurde im Juli 1913 entlassen. Am 4. Dezember 1912 heiratete er Laura Mary Seward in Springfield, Vermont; diese Ehe endete mit der Scheidung. Im Juni 1917 war er Briefträger beim U.S. Post Office in Bridgeport, Connecticut, und wohnte an der Adresse 276 Gregory Street. Spätestens 1926 war er wieder in Springfield, und am 11. August 1926 heiratete er in Chester, Vermont, Mary Abbie West aus Chester Depot. Die Tochter Gwendolyn wurde 1927 geboren, Richard 1930 und Alma später. 1942 wohnte er an der Adresse 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, und arbeitete für das U.S. Post Office Department, Main Street, Springfield; 1950 war er 62 und lebte in Springfield. Die Karte, die in der Vermont-Serie auf seine Karte von 1942 folgt, wahrscheinlich deren Rückseite, beschreibt einen Mann von 5 Fuß 7 Zoll Größe und 142 Pfund, mit blauen Augen und braunem Haar. Er starb am 22. Mai 1966 im DeGoesbriand Memorial Hospital in Burlington, Vermont, im Alter von 78 Jahren, im Ruhestand und wohnhaft an der Adresse 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, und seine Sterbeurkunde nennt seine Frau als Mary Abbie. people.story: Mary Abbie West, called Abby in the family, was born in Peru, Vermont, in 1901 or 1902, the daughter of William Wallace West and Alice Dina Waite (born in Dorset, Vermont), according to her 1926 marriage card. She was living at Chester Depot, and is probably the Abbie West paid for teaching in the Chester schools that year, when on August 11, 1926 she married Harry James Farr at Chester; it was her first marriage and his second. She was the mother of Gwendolyn (born July 1, 1927), Richard (born July 1, 1930) and Alma; both children's birth cards give her place of birth as Peru, Vermont. In 1942 Harry named her as the person who would always know his address, and in 1950 she worked as a clerk at the post office in Springfield. Her husband's 1966 death certificate names her as his wife. Family tradition: West relatives remembered a farm in Wells, Maine. That place is not on the map. [^s27] [^s05] [^s36] [^s41] [^s40] [^s49] [^s50] [^s55] [^s57]
people.story_de: Mary Abbie West, in der Familie Abby genannt, wurde 1901 oder 1902 in Peru, Vermont, geboren, als Tochter von William Wallace West und Alice Dina Waite (geboren in Dorset, Vermont), laut ihrer Heiratskarte von 1926. Sie lebte in Chester Depot und ist wahrscheinlich die Abbie West, die in jenem Jahr für den Unterricht an den Schulen in Chester bezahlt wurde, als sie am 11. August 1926 in Chester Harry James Farr heiratete; es war ihre erste Ehe und seine zweite. Sie war die Mutter von Gwendolyn (geboren am 1. Juli 1927), Richard (geboren am 1. Juli 1930) und Alma; die Geburtskarten beider Kinder geben als Geburtsort der Mutter Peru, Vermont, an. 1942 nannte Harry sie als die Person, die seine Anschrift immer kennen würde, und 1950 arbeitete sie als Angestellte im Postamt in Springfield. Die Sterbeurkunde ihres Mannes von 1966 nennt sie als seine Ehefrau. Familientradition: Verwandte der Familie West erinnerten sich an einen Hof in Wells, Maine. Dieser Ort steht nicht auf der Karte. people.story: Roy E. Crosby was born on February 25, 1925 and raised in Chicopee, Massachusetts, one of at least nine children of Ernest and Eva (Pierce) Crosby. In the Second World War he served in the U.S. Navy aboard the escort carrier Marcus Island and fought in the Battle of Leyte Gulf in October 1944. He married Dorothy Richardson, and in 1950 they moved to West Springfield, where they raised Robert, Debra, Rick and Lynn. Roy worked as a pressman for the Springfield Newspapers, where he also played AA ball, and finished his career as an HVAC technician at Western New England College. A lifelong Yankees fan, he built a summer home on Otis Reservoir with his family. He died at home on May 2, 2014 after 65 years of marriage and was buried with military honors at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s20] [^s21] [^s23] [^s24]

Er heiratete Dorothy Richardson, und 1950 zogen sie nach West Springfield, wo sie Robert, Debra, Rick und Lynn großzogen. Roy arbeitete als Druckmaschinenführer bei den Springfield Newspapers, wo er auch Baseball der Klasse AA spielte, und beendete seine Laufbahn als HLK-Techniker am Western New England College. Als lebenslanger Anhänger der Yankees baute er mit seiner Familie ein Sommerhaus am Otis Reservoir. Er starb am 2. Mai 2014 zu Hause nach 65 Ehejahren und wurde mit militärischen Ehren auf dem Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam beigesetzt. [^s20] [^s21] [^s23] [^s24]

people.story: Ernest Allan Crosby was born at Norwood, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, probably on June 1, 1884 (his 1918 draft card; his 1942 card writes the date as 1/6/1884), the son of James W. and Asenath (Porter) Crosby. Like many young people from Yarmouth County he moved to Massachusetts, and on July 6, 1906, aged 22, he married Eva E. Pierce of Brazil Lake at Wakefield. Their first child, Ruby Evelyn, was born in Wakefield that November. On September 12, 1918 he registered for the draft at Chicopee, living on Luther Street, with Eva Etta Crosby as his nearest relative. The family settled in Chicopee, where they raised at least nine children: Esther, Ruby, Winston, Ivoline, Thelma, Gordon, Muriel, Roy and Bernard. In 1942, aged 57, he lived at 35 Haven Avenue, Chicopee, worked for the A. G. Spalding Company, and named Mrs. Eva Crosby as the person who would always know his address. Eva died in 1944. In the 1950 census Ernest, then 65 and widowed, was still in Chicopee with his daughter Thelma, and with his daughter Muriel and her husband Douglas Rhodes. He died in 1958 and is buried beside Eva in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield. [^s28] [^s04] [^s22] [^s23] [^s54] [^s56]
people.story_de: Ernest Allan Crosby wurde in Norwood, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia (Neuschottland), wahrscheinlich am 1. Juni 1884 geboren (seine Musterungskarte von 1918; seine Karte von 1942 schreibt das Datum als 1/6/1884), als Sohn von James W. und Asenath (Porter) Crosby. Wie viele junge Leute aus Yarmouth County zog er nach Massachusetts und heiratete am 6. Juli 1906, im Alter von 22 Jahren, Eva E. Pierce aus Brazil Lake in Wakefield. Ihr erstes Kind, Ruby Evelyn, wurde im November desselben Jahres in Wakefield geboren. Am 12. September 1918 meldete er sich in Chicopee zur Musterung. Er wohnte in der Luther Street und gab Eva Etta Crosby als nächste Angehörige an. Die Familie ließ sich in Chicopee nieder, wo sie mindestens neun Kinder großzog: Esther, Ruby, Winston, Ivoline, Thelma, Gordon, Muriel, Roy und Bernard. 1942, im Alter von 57 Jahren, lebte er unter der Adresse 35 Haven Avenue, Chicopee, arbeitete für die A. G. Spalding Company und nannte Mrs. Eva Crosby als die Person, die seine Anschrift immer kennen würde. Eva starb 1944. In der Volkszählung von 1950 war Ernest, damals 65 und verwitwet, noch in Chicopee, mit seiner Tochter Thelma sowie mit seiner Tochter Muriel und deren Ehemann Douglas Rhodes. Er starb 1958 und ist neben Eva auf dem Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield, beigesetzt. [^s28] [^s04] [^s22] [^s23] [^s54] [^s56]

people.story: Eva E. Pierce was born about 1885 at Brazil Lake, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, the daughter of Charles and Alice Pierce. She married Ernest A. Crosby, a neighbor from nearby Norwood, at Wakefield, Massachusetts, on July 6, 1906, and their daughter Ruby was born there that November. She raised a large family in Chicopee and died in 1944. She is buried in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield, Massachusetts. [^s28] [^s22] [^s23] Her husband's 1918 draft card names his nearest relative as Eva Etta Crosby, which gives her middle name. [^s54]
people.story_de: Eva E. Pierce wurde um 1885 in Brazil Lake, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia (Neuschottland), als Tochter von Charles und Alice Pierce geboren. Sie heiratete am 6. Juli 1906 in Wakefield, Massachusetts, Ernest A. Crosby, einen Nachbarn aus dem nahen Norwood, und ihre Tochter Ruby wurde dort im November desselben Jahres geboren. Sie zog in Chicopee eine große Familie groß und starb 1944. Sie ist auf dem Hillcrest Park Cemetery in Springfield, Massachusetts, begraben. [^s28] [^s22] [^s23] Die Musterungskarte ihres Mannes von 1918 nennt als nächste Angehörige Eva Etta Crosby und gibt damit ihren Mittelnamen an. [^s54]

people.story: Richard H. Farr was born in Springfield, Vermont, on July 1, 1930, the son of Harry James Farr and Mary Abbie West Farr. He served in the U.S. Navy from 1948 to 1952, married Doris Ann Elliott. Her details are not published. He lived on Cape Ann in Massachusetts. He died at Rockport on May 11, 2009, survived by his sisters Alma and Gwendolyn, and was buried privately in Springfield, Vermont. [^s27] His Vermont birth record, found in November 2026, confirms that he was born on July 1, 1930 at Springfield Hospital, the second child of Harry J. Farr and Mary Abbie West. [^s51]

people.story: Barbara Eleanor Richardson was born on October 26, 1921 in Cochituate, a village of Wayland, Massachusetts, the elder daughter of Robert H. and Anna E. (Ernst) Richardson. She married Roland Vogel, lived for many years in Chicopee and worked as an insurance agent for Palmer, Goodell and Keeney. Skier, golfer, swimmer and square dancer, she spent more than 50 summers on Otis Reservoir. She died on November 24, 2016, survived by her sister Dorothy "Ducky" Crosby, and was buried at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s35] [^s33]
